THE DEFECT, measured yesterday on the live system. The queue dropped below target
(5/6), queue_status correctly said should_outreach=True — and the tick planned ZERO
outreach actions. Why: server/pipeline/loop_runner.py assemble_world hard-codes
  "candidates": [],
  "referrals": [],
(~line 97). The vetting and ranking modules (candidate_vetting.evaluate_candidate /
rank_candidates) are fully built and tested; nothing feeds them. The owner calls this
the defect class the repo exists to kill: finished is not connected.

Also measured: three solo episodes (episode_type "solo", no guests) were flagged
stalled by pipeline_queue.is_stalled with "no response data recorded" — a solo has no
guest whose silence can stall it. They are currently patched around with
awaiting_first_contact; the semantics belong in the module.

THE FIX, three parts:

1. server/pipeline/candidate_ingest.py (new). File-based candidate feed with three
   merge sources, ALL under the episodes dir so the world assembly stays one-rooted:
     load_candidate_feed(episodes_dir, *, now) -> {"candidates": [...], "provenance": {...}, "problems": [...]}
   Sources, merged in this priority order with dedup by normalized email (fall back
   to normalized name when no email):
     a) episodes/CANDIDATE-INBOX.json — manual/inbound drops. Schema
        {"schema": "candidate-inbox-v1", "candidates": [{name, email?, source,
        topic_hint?, evidence?}]}. Malformed file or wrong schema: feed still loads
        from other sources, and the problem is recorded in "problems" — never raise,
        never silently drop.
     b) episodes/REFERRALS.json (schema referral-ledger-v1, already exists in the
        repo root's episodes dir — READ IT to match its real shape). Referral entries
        in the "referrals" list become candidates ONLY when their state is
        "introduced" or later — the owner's rule is referrer introduces first; a
        merely-named person must NOT become an outreach target. Asks in the "asks"
        list never become candidates.
     c) past guests: episodes/*/episode.json with a published/complete-class stage
        and a guest email — candidate kind "past_guest_reinvite", eligible only when
        their episode published more than 180 days before `now` (no pestering recent
        guests). Read the stage sets from pipeline_queue rather than inventing new
        ones.
   Each emitted candidate carries: name, email (may be None), kind
   (inbound|referral_introduced|past_guest_reinvite), source_evidence (where it came
   from: file + index or episode id), first_seen (ISO from `now` on first emit).
   Deterministic ordering (sort by kind then name). The provenance dict counts per
   source; the function NEVER raises on bad input.

2. server/pipeline/loop_runner.py: assemble_world calls load_candidate_feed and fills
   "candidates" and "referrals" (referrals = the full referral-ledger records list,
   so referral_lifecycle logic downstream sees real state; keep [] only when the
   ledger file is absent). Feed problems land in the existing load_errors mechanism
   so a corrupt feed is VISIBLE in every tick summary. Do not change any other world
   key or the function signature.

3. server/pipeline/pipeline_queue.py is_stalled: an episode whose episode_type is
   "solo" (no guests to go silent) cannot be guest-stalled — return (False, "") the
   same way _GUEST_DONE_STAGES already short-circuits, with a comment naming the
   incident (three scaffolded solos false-flagged 2026-07-31). Everything else about
   is_stalled stays byte-identical — the fail-closed rules for guest episodes are
   load-bearing and tested.

TESTS (tests/test_candidate_feed_wiring.py; at least 8, tmp episodes dirs):
 (1) THE DEFECT CLOSED: a world assembled over a dir with a valid CANDIDATE-INBOX
     entry yields world["candidates"] non-empty, and plan_tick on a below-target
     queue now plans a candidate_outreach action (import loop_tick and prove the
     end-to-end connection — this is the test that fails on yesterday's code);
 (2) referral in state "recorded" (named but NOT introduced) does NOT become a
     candidate; the same referral in state "introduced" DOES — the owner's
     introduce-first rule enforced at the feed;
 (3) past guest published 200+ days ago becomes past_guest_reinvite; one published
     30 days ago does not;
 (4) NEGATIVE: malformed CANDIDATE-INBOX.json (bad JSON) -> other sources still
     load, problems non-empty, and assemble_world surfaces it in load_errors;
 (5) NEGATIVE: unknown schema string in the inbox file -> recorded problem, no
     candidates from that file;
 (6) dedup: same email arriving from inbox and past-guest sources yields ONE
     candidate, and the higher-priority (inbox) provenance wins;
 (7) solo episode with no response data is NOT stalled; an identical guest episode
     IS — the exemption is exactly episode_type solo;
 (8) determinism: identical inputs -> identical candidate list including order;
 (9) NEGATIVE: an ask in REFERRALS.json asks list never appears as a candidate.
Keep tests/test_pipeline_queue.py, tests/test_loop_runner.py, tests/test_loop_tick.py green.

Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Edit files there directly. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls, no posting anywhere — this is a PLANNER; execution stays behind the send gateway.

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production change with no tests, fewer than 7 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these; the test file is new):
  server/pipeline/promo_schedule.py
  server/pipeline/loop_tick.py
  tests/test_weekly_drumbeat.py

THE OWNER'S COMPLAINT, verbatim intent: promotion must be "regular and continuous
attention", not launch-day-only. Measured reality: promo_schedule plans 3 touches
during an episode's launch week and then NOTHING, ever. Episodes published in June
(three of them, all with clips and social drafts on disk) have had zero promotional
touches since their launch week. The back catalog is dead weight the system already
paid to produce.

THE FIX — extend the planner, keep every existing safety property:

1. In server/pipeline/promo_schedule.py add:
     plan_weekly_drumbeat(episodes, *, now, history) -> dict
   READ THE MODULE FIRST and reuse its existing touch/asset vocabulary and its
   distinct-assets rule rather than inventing a parallel one.
   The plan for the 7 days starting at `now`:
     a) LAUNCH-WEEK touches: episodes whose publish_date falls inside the window (or
        whose launch week is still in progress) get the existing TOUCHES_PER_WEEK=3
        treatment — delegate to the existing planning logic, do not fork it.
     b) EVERGREEN touch: exactly ONE back-catalog episode per week — published,
        outside its launch week, chosen as the one whose last promotional touch is
        OLDEST according to `history` (never-touched counts as oldest; tie-break by
        older publish_date, then episode id, so rotation is total and deterministic).
        The touch names a concrete asset that exists for that episode (a clip file,
        the social-image, or a quote from its social drafts — the planner receives
        what assets each episode has via the episode records; a back-catalog episode
        with NO assets on record is reported in "skipped" with reason
        asset_missing, never invented).
     c) `history` is a dict episode_id -> last_touched ISO string. The FUNCTION does
        not do IO. Missing/empty history means nothing was ever touched — plan the
        oldest published episode, and record in the plan that history was empty
        (visible assumption, not silence).
   Return {"week_start", "entries": [{date, episode_id, kind:
   launch_touch|evergreen_touch, asset, why}], "skipped": [{episode_id, reason}]}
   — every entry carries "why", every omission is named. Deterministic.

2. In server/pipeline/loop_tick.py, plan_tick's promo section: call the drumbeat
   planner so the tick's planned actions include the week's touches as DRAFT-CLASS
   actions routed exactly like the existing promo actions (same action envelope,
   same gateway discipline — a planned touch is a draft for the send lane, never a
   direct post). The tick must include the evergreen touch even when no episode
   launched this week — that is the whole point. History comes from the world's
   episode records (each episode.json may carry promo_touch_history; absent means
   never touched — read what exists, do not invent a new file).

TESTS (tests/test_weekly_drumbeat.py; at least 7, fixed `now` everywhere):
 (1) THE COMPLAINT CLOSED: three published episodes, none in launch week, empty
     history -> the weekly plan contains exactly ONE evergreen touch naming the
     oldest-published episode and a real asset;
 (2) rotation: history showing episode A touched last week -> episode B (next
     oldest) is chosen; running 3 consecutive weeks (feeding each plan back into
     history) touches 3 distinct episodes — no favorite-episode loop;
 (3) launch week + back catalog together -> 3 launch touches for the launching
     episode AND 1 evergreen for the catalog, 4 dated entries in the window;
 (4) NEGATIVE: a back-catalog episode with no assets on record lands in skipped
     with asset_missing and is never given an invented asset;
 (5) NEGATIVE: an unpublished episode is never planned for evergreen;
 (6) plan_tick output includes the drumbeat actions in the standard action envelope
     (assert the same envelope keys as existing promo actions, and that dry-run
     planning performs nothing);
 (7) determinism: identical inputs -> identical plans;
 (8) an episode in its launch week is excluded from evergreen selection (no
     double-dipping).
Keep tests/test_promo_schedule.py and tests/test_loop_tick.py green.
